name: dotnet-service
description: An ASP.NET Core web API or web app (.NET 6+), optionally serving a built frontend from the same process.

runtimes.version: <the target framework moniker in the .csproj, e.g. net8.0>
runtimes.provision: <the matching .NET runtime/SDK installed on dev and prod hosts>

build.what: Frontend bundle, if the app serves one

services.manager: <a service manager or a container runtime>
services.bind: <loopback-only, unless a trusted edge forwards identity>
services.health: <a real health endpoint, e.g. /health via a health-checks middleware>

routing.staticRoot: <built frontend output folder, if any, or wwwroot>

files: <a per-environment settings file, kept out of version control for real environments>
config.rule: real settings files are gitignored; a committed example settings file shows the shape only

data.migrations: <the app's migration tool, e.g. an ORM's migrations feature, or none>
data.state: <an external database; nothing durable lives on the app host itself>

ci.workflow: <CI workflow file: restore, build, test, publish>

verify: the health endpoint returns a body with a status field, not just HTTP 200
a rendered page or the frontend bundle's hash changed, so an old bundle behind a new backend cannot pass
